correctness.rationale: All 1416 faces of the bidirected K(2,6) multipath complex are reconstructed from directed indegree/outdegree and no-directed-cycle constraints. A 793-operation witness exhaustively gives 623 free-face pairs, one critical 0-simplex and 169 critical 3-simplices, no critical cells in degrees 1 or 2. The standalone verifier checks each free face is unique and its coface maximal in the remaining complex, verifies acyclicity of the reversed-incidence Hasse graph, and recomputes mod-two Betti vectors for n=1,...,6. Forman discrete-Morse theory then proves the integral wedge of 169 three-spheres; smaller n each has nonzero reduced mod-two homology below degree 3, excluding two-connectedness.

The full relevant mathematical sections and stated theorems of the two primary arXiv papers were compared at the level of graph orientation, face definition, parameter domain, and conclusion; the searched public results include no stronger covering theorem. value.rationale: The first two-connected case in a canonical two-hub bidirected biclique family is an exact, motivated finite connectivity cutoff, not a generic table entry. The originating 2026 literature emphasizes connectivity and unresolved sphere-wedge types for bidirected graph multipath complexes; this related, genuinely cyclic family exhibits a sharp low-degree homology-to-two-connectivity transition and an explicit integral wedge decomposition not inferred from an Euler characteristic. The result is restricted to this natural finite cutoff and does not assert a larger family theorem.
